events.subtitle: Farewell Tour
events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents The Bad Plus Farewell Tour on October 17-19, 2026 with the current quartet of David King, Reid Anderson, Ben Monder and Chris Speed. October 17 and 18 have sets starting at 4:30 PM and 7:30 PM; October 19 has sets starting at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM. Blue Note Tokyo lists a ¥9,500 music charge and describes the engagement as a farewell live performance marking the end of the band's history. The Bad Plus' official site separately states that 2026 is the final year of The Bad Plus and that the group will perform final shows throughout the year.

en.why_it_matters: The farewell is the live argument: this is one of the Tokyo chances to hear the Anderson-King core with Ben Monder and Chris Speed before The Bad Plus closes its final year. The quartet's guitar-and-saxophone front line turned a band once defined by piano-trio disruption into a different kind of collision between jazz improvisation, rock weight and compositional structure, so the ending captures a genuinely specific chapter rather than a generic legacy visit.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the six sets if October 17-19 overlaps a Tokyo stay and let Minami-Aoyama anchor that evening. Three nights create enough flexibility to fit the farewell into a broader Kanto itinerary without rebuilding a Japan trip around a single curtain time.

es.why_it_matters: La despedida es el argumento en vivo: ésta es una de las oportunidades en Tokio para escuchar al núcleo Anderson-King con Ben Monder y Chris Speed antes de que The Bad Plus cierre su último año. El frente de guitarra y saxofón transformó a una banda antes definida por la ruptura del piano trío en otra clase de choque entre improvisación de jazz, peso rockero y estructura compositiva, así que el cierre captura un capítulo realmente específico y no una visita de legado genérica.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los seis sets si del 17 al 19 de octubre coincide con una estancia en Tokio y dejaría que Minami-Aoyama ordene esa noche. Tres noches dan suficiente flexibilidad para integrar la despedida en un itinerario más amplio por Kanto sin reconstruir un viaje a Japón alrededor de una sola función.
